title: Instance-adaptive TS augmentation (playbook plan)
method: A parametric augmentation network learns per-instance views: a factorization mask h (hard-concrete relaxed Bernoulli per time step from a factorization head), a non-zero transformation mask g (transformation head) and noise η (random time-step masking of the encoder's first hidden layer); both heads share an input layer and a dilated-CNN extractor. The augmenter is trained with a Principle-of-Relevant-Information objective (β·expected L0 of h + mean-embedding discrepancy through the encoder) plus a temporal-consistency loss L_t (λ); the encoder is trained with L_global (InfoNCE) + α·L_local (subsequence contrast). Both are trained from scratch, alternating GAN-style (encoder every step, augmenter every M rounds), each with its own Adam optimizer.

compute.hardware: 8x 40 GB GPUs (single machine); planned at 80% of 4,032 nominal GPU-h

outOfScope.reason: needs a separate streaming, point-adjusted protocol with threshold-selection leakage risks, and does not fit the budget; C1b is narrowed to forecasting + classification

claims.text: Factorization-based information-theoretic definition of good views; Theorems 1-3
Good views preserve task-relevant information while adding variance, without domain knowledge (narrowed to forecasting and classification)
The parametric instantiation learns per-instance augmentations
Avoids ad-hoc choice / trial-and-error tuning of augmentations
Common augmentations (crop, scaling, ...) are special cases
Beats existing TS representation learning on forecasting (uni + multi) and classification

questions.text: Forecasting: does ours lower MSE relative to each re-run baseline on the 4 main datasets × 5 horizons, separately for univariate and multivariate?
questions.hypothesis: Ours lowers MSE relative to each re-run baseline, separately for uni and multi; the headline comparator is the strongest baseline per setting selected on val, and TS2Vec counts as the better of its iteration-matched and compute-matched arms
questions.predictionIfFalse: The test fails, or the reduction is < 2%, or ours is significantly worse in any horizon group
questions.minEffect: ≥ max(2%, 2×SE) mean relative MSE reduction over the 20 (dataset × horizon) cells; sign-flip permutation p < 0.05 after Holm; point estimate > 0 under leave-one-dataset-out; claims worded per horizon group (short {24, 48}, long {≥168 / ≥288}), a group that does not pass on its own is excluded

questions.text: Classification: does ours have higher mean accuracy than every re-run baseline on UCR-128 and UEA-30?
questions.hypothesis: On UCR-128 and UEA-30, ours has higher mean accuracy than every re-run baseline (also reported on UCR-98 / UEA-20, excluding the tuning datasets)
questions.predictionIfFalse: Gain < 0.5 pt or not significant on either archive
questions.minEffect: ≥ +1.0 pt mean accuracy on each archive, Wilcoxon over datasets with Holm-p < 0.05

questions.text: With the same encoder and the same L_con, is untuned-default ours (0 tuning trials) non-inferior to L_con + the hand-picked augmentation grid (21 configs, selected per task family on T val)?
questions.hypothesis: Untuned-default ours is non-inferior to the tuned grid in every task family and ≥ loss-only (L_con + TS2Vec default augs); secondary: tuned ours vs tuned grid as a superiority test
questions.predictionIfFalse: The grid beats untuned ours beyond the margin in any family
questions.minEffect: Non-inferiority margin −1% MSE / −0.5 pt accuracy; the one-sided 95% CI lower bound must exceed the margin in every task family

questions.text: With configs frozen, does the gap vs the grid hold under transfer: cross-domain (Weather, ETTm2), cross-archive (UCR-tuned configs on the 20 untuned UEA datasets) and within-archive (UCR-98, UEA-20)?
questions.hypothesis: 'No domain knowledge' is claimed only if Q3a holds and ours keeps a ≥0 gap vs the grid on the cross-domain/cross-archive sets; within-archive results are reported as within-archive transfer only
questions.predictionIfFalse: The gap shrinks by more than half relative to the tuning subset, or turns negative cross-domain

questions.text: Tuning cost: untuned ours spends 0 tuning GPU-h vs the grid's measured enumeration cost (≈84 GPU-h on T)
questions.hypothesis: Equal quality with zero tuning; holds only if Q3a holds
questions.notes: Pre-registered as expected-false: tuned ours is cheaper to tune per trial than the grid (ours costs ≈2× per trial), so this is reported but not claimed

questions.text: Do learned per-instance masks beat random masks matched in sparsity and scale, a dataset-level learned mask, and RandAugment-style per-instance random composition under L_con?
questions.hypothesis: Learned per-instance masks beat each of the three controls
questions.predictionIfFalse: Any control is within the threshold in both families
questions.minEffect: ≥ max(1% MSE / 0.5 pt, 2×SE) over each control, per task family

questions.text: Does adding our module improve each backbone over its own augmentations, with equal trials within each pair (forecasting: TS2Vec, CoST, Transformer-TS2Vec; classification: TS2Vec, TS-TCC, Transformer-TS2Vec)?
questions.hypothesis: Adding our module improves each backbone over its own augmentations
questions.predictionIfFalse: Improvement in ≤1 of 3 pairs in both families
questions.minEffect: ≥ max(1% MSE / 0.5 pt, 2×SE) per pair, Holm within the Q5 family

questions.text: Theorem 1 vs a known regularizer: are invertible-only views (no η) worse than the default hidden-layer masking η and than an input-jitter η matched in view diversity?
questions.hypothesis: No-η views are worse than default η and worse than input Gaussian jitter (σ matched on S1 val to the default's view diversity); the jitter variant recovers ≥50% of the default's gain over no-η
questions.predictionIfFalse: No-η is not worse, or the jitter variant recovers < 50% (then the effect is attributed to TS2Vec-style masking regularization, not Theorem 1)

questions.text: Label preservation: how much accuracy does a supervised probe lose on views (input-space partial view v* with an input-space classifier; full view v with a same-architecture classifier and η at its first-layer output)?
questions.hypothesis: Ours drops ≤2 pt; adversarial-swap and LEAVES-style views drop ≥2 pt more
questions.predictionIfFalse: Our drop is not smaller than adversarial

questions.text: Diversity / Theorem 3 (encoder-independent): k-NN entropy and within-instance view distance, in input space for v* and in a frozen, randomly initialised, fixed-seed first layer for v
questions.hypothesis: Ĥ(v) − Ĥ(x) ≥ 0 for ours, and greater than for no-η views

questions.text: Does PRI beat the adversarial objective swap (S3-1) and LEAVES (S2-10)?
questions.hypothesis: PRI beats the adversarial objective swap and LEAVES
questions.predictionIfFalse: Adversarial or LEAVES ≥ PRI (S3 rule: drop the 'PRI instead of adversarial' claim)

questions.text: On a synthetic dataset with a planted label-relevant segment, does h recover it?

statistics.variance: t-CI over cells (forecasting); one-sided 95% CI for non-inferiority

statistics.notes: 5 seeds on main cells, Q5 pairs and gating ablations; untuned ours 3 seeds; 3 on other ablations and sweeps. Every minimum effect is max(stated %, 2×SE of the paired difference); effects passing the test but below 2×SE are 'inconclusive'. Escalation: if the S1 forecasting effect is below 2× its paired SD, S2 forecasting goes to 8 seeds for the 9 forecasting arms (+210 GPU-h from reserve).
